answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should tie reputation to costly, verifiable work rather than free identities. Like a trellis that only supports vines that climb it, a network can require agents to earn trust through repeated, attested contributions before gaining influence. New identities may wander in freely, but they start at the inlet with almost no weight: they can observe and do small tasks, yet voting power and rewards grow only after a history of useful, checkable work. Copying an identity then buys nothing, because influence follows proven effort, not the number of accounts.
